text:
leah: Hey @tom @raj — AcmeHealth returned the DPA with a couple items that could block final sign-off: they want (1) a simple dataflow diagram showing where embeddings and user content live, (2) confirmation on whether we ever store raw PII in embeddings, and (3) KMS key provenance for BYOK. Can engineering/security give a short, customer-facing answer? They asked for this by EOD.

onboard-bot: Ticket #CH-8247 created and assigned to customer-success (leah). Reminder: SLA = 48h.

tom: thx. quick q — are they using hosted API (redwood cloud) or dedicated? that changes the BYOK answer.

leah: hosted for now, may move to Dedicated next quarter.

mike: short answer from eng: we do NOT include raw PII inside embedding vectors as a separate persisted object. We store models' token outputs and embedding vectors in our managed blob store for retrieval/TTL purposes, but embedding vectors are not reversible to original text with any practical attack (per current crypto/ML literature). retention: embeddings TTL = 90 days by default, configurable per-customer.

raj: security note: add that customers can request BYOK only on Dedicated/Private. For hosted, keys are KMS-managed by Redwood; we can provide KMS key provenance logs for the service account that generated encryption keys. Also: mention redaction guidance — customers should mask direct identifiers before sending if they require strict PII controls.

tom: drafting a one-paragraph reply for Leah to send to customer. PTAL and I'll adjust.

mike: lgtm; add the retention and SLOs for deletion (we surface deletion in our audit logs within 24hrs of request).

raj: +1. Also include a link to SOC2 controls mapping for data handling: https://redwood.example.com/security/soc2-data-handling (customer-facing).

leah: Draft reply (please copy/paste):
"Hi — thanks for the questions. Short answers: we do not store raw PII as a separate reversible artifact; embeddings are stored as numeric vectors in our managed store (default TTL 90 days, configurable). For hosted deployments, encryption keys are managed by Redwood KMS; BYOK is available for Dedicated/Private only — we can provide KMS key provenance and audit logs on request. We recommend pseudonymizing direct identifiers if you require strict minimization. Attached is a simple dataflow snapshot and the SOC2 data handling doc. Happy to hop on a quick call if helpful. — Leah, Customer Success"

leah: Attached ASCII dataflow for their diagram: 
```
user -> redwood-api -> tokenizer -> model -> embedding-store (encrypted, TTL=90d)
                     \-> ephemeral logs (48h)
backup -> encrypted-blob-storage (access via KMS)
```

tom: I tweaked phrasing a bit; SGTM. raj, mike — any other red flags before I send?

raj: Add: we never log full request bodies to long-term logs; only minimal metadata for billing/metrics. Also say we can sign a narrow addendum to the DPA for embeddings retention if they need it.

mike: confirm we can generate the KMS provenance snapshot — ops can export within 48 hours.

leah: Perfect. I'll send this now and mark the onboarding as "evidence requested" on the renewal tracker. Thanks all :heart:
